speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me which specific antibiotic you were prescribed and when you started it? Also, how many days ago did these symptoms begin?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diagnosed with acute sinusitis one week ago, no known history of adverse drug reactions, immunizations up to date. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Patient
text: No additional symptoms mentioned. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS).

The clinical picture of fever, rash, and joint pain immediately following antibiotic use is highly suggestive of SJS or Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS). I am requesting images of the rash to confirm the extent and morphology of the skin involvement.
